subject: Archaeology
title: Gertrude Bell and Iraq's Antiquities Law
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Gertrude Bell and Iraq's Antiquities Law.

hook.text: A British woman drew the borders of Iraq, founded its national museum, and wrote the law that stopped artifact looting.

buildup.text: Gertrude Bell was an archaeologist, spy, and political advisor. She helped create modern Iraq after World War I.

discovery.text: She wrote Iraq's Antiquities Law in 1924, keeping Iraqi artifacts in Iraq — ending the colonial practice of shipping them abroad.

twist.text: Other countries copied her model. Egypt, Turkey, and Greece all adopted similar laws to protect their own heritage.

climax.text: Bell founded the Iraq Museum in Baghdad, filling it with treasures from Ur, Babylon, and Nineveh.

punchline.text: She drew a nation's borders and saved its history. Few people remember her name.

quiz.question: What did Gertrude Bell's Antiquities Law accomplish?
options: It banned all foreign archaeologists from working in Iraq
It kept Iraqi artifacts in Iraq — ending the colonial export of antiquities
It established English as the official language for archaeological reports
